title: EdTech, AI, and Teaching Series - Part 3: Blended Learning That Works
author: K. Andy
summary: Andy argues that successful AI integration requires intentional instructional structure, not just tools. Blended learning models, particularly station rotation, provide the framework needed for safe and effective AI use. The article advocates for three rotating stations: teacher-led instruction (direct teaching, guided practice), collaborative work (discussion, application), and independent/online work (where AI is bounded and purposeful). This structure aligns with cognitive science research while managing AI risks through time-limited, supervised use. Andy emphasizes that structure transforms AI from an open-ended risk into a managed instructional resource and increases teacher efficacy by enabling small-group work and closer observation.
points: Structure is the missing piece in AI initiatives: Technology fails when introduced without clear instructional purpose. Blended learning provides the organizational framework that makes AI integration safe and effective.

Station rotation aligns with research-based instruction: Teacher-led stations support Rosenshine's principles; collaborative stations enable elaboration and retrieval practice; independent stations bound AI use with clear expectations.
Bounded AI use is safer and more effective: When AI is time-limited, supervised, and aligned to learning goals, it functions as a support tool rather than a replacement for thinking or instruction.

Blended learning increases teacher efficacy: Small-group instruction enables observation, adjustment, and relationship-building. Teachers feel more effective when they manage routines and respond to individual needs.
Innovation becomes sustainable through structure: Blended learning allows schools to integrate technology without abandoning proven teaching practices.
quotes: The answer is not another tool or platform. It is structure.
Blended learning is active, engaged learning online combined with active, engaged learning offline to give students more control over the time, place, pace, and path of their learning.
When bounded by clear expectations and instructional goals, AI can support scaffolded practice, clarification of misunderstandings, organization of ideas, and formative feedback.
Blended learning transforms AI from an open-ended risk into a managed instructional resource.
